atlas_home_region_card.compact: Groove-first soul music where rhythm, bass, and band hits become the main event.
atlas_home_region_card.standard: It became a foundation for disco, hip-hop sampling, dance music, and modern R&B rhythm.
atlas_home_region_card.deep: Groove-first soul music where rhythm, bass, and band hits become the main event. It became a foundation for disco, hip-hop sampling, dance music, and modern R&B rhythm.

region_scene_page.compact: Funk grew from soul and R&B by pushing syncopation, bass, drums, and collective groove to the front, then expanded through psychedelic soul and cosmic stagecraft.
region_scene_page.standard: Funk grew from soul and R&B by pushing syncopation, bass, drums, and collective groove to the front, then expanded through psychedelic soul and cosmic stagecraft. James Brown's I Got You (I Feel Good), Sly & the Family Stone's Dance to the Music, Curtis Mayfield's Superfly, and Kool & the Gang's Jungle Boogie give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Funk grew from soul and R&B by pushing syncopation, bass, drums, and collective groove to the front, then expanded through psychedelic soul and cosmic stagecraft. The groove does not support the song; the groove is the song. James Brown's I Got You (I Feel Good), Sly & the Family Stone's Dance to the Music, Curtis Mayfield's Superfly, and Kool & the Gang's Jungle Boogie give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
